_comment: Single source of truth for per-platform facts. Consumers derive from this file;
nothing downstream restates a value that appears here.
panel.source records provenance and ranks: hardware > docs/devel/printers/*_SUPPORT.md
> docs/devel/printer-research/*. Where a doc and hardware disagree, hardware wins and
the doc is corrected in the same change. A panel with no hardware behind it carries
"verified": false so the gate can report what is still doc-derived.
panel is the only geometry input. Effective resolution, splash size class and printer
image size are DERIVED (see include/prerender_size_class.h and
scripts/platform_manifest.py), never stored, because K1 and K2 are portrait panels
used rotated and a stored effective size loses that distinction.

storage.state_root is where cache/ and logs/ live. It is never the payload root nor inside it: the payload is what an update replaces, and Moonraker's type:web entry rmtree()s it before extracting. cache_dir and log_file stay authoritative per platform because AD5X deliberately splits them - its log has to land where the mod's archiver looks.

storage.previous_root and previous_state_root declare where a platform used to keep its payload and state. An install found at previous_root is migrated to root rather than adopted, so a relocation is a manifest edit. Both stay in HELIX_INSTALL_DIRS and kInstallRoots for as long as unmigrated devices exist, because the updater, the debug bundle collector and uninstall all have to keep finding them.
Size class names are the UiBreakpoint tiers from include/ui_breakpoint.h.
The pre-render size-class ladder, as data. Classes are the UiBreakpoint tiers from
include/ui_breakpoint.h and the thresholds are its UI_BREAKPOINT_*_MAX values, so an
asset filename and a layout override mean the same thing by the same word.
max_narrow is min(width, height): a full-screen canvas has to fit the cramped axis,
which is what breakpoint_for() keys off. Rules are evaluated in order, first match
wins, and an absent bound means unbounded on that side.
Two departures from a plain tier lookup. A wide, short bar display takes `ultrawide`
because its canvas shape is unlike anything else at its tier. And nothing is composited
above `xlarge`, so the last rule is a catch-all and a larger panel scales.
src/system/prerender_size_class.cpp is the compiled implementation and
scripts/platform_manifest.py the build-time one; tests/unit/test_prerender_size_class.cpp
asserts both agree with these rules and that the thresholds still match ui_breakpoint.h.

storage.notes: /opt is on the 240MB overlay mounted at /; /mnt/UDISK is the 27.5GB user partition, and both the payload and its state live there.

panel.notes: The tiny class composites at 480x320, 48px taller than this panel. get_splash_3d_target_height lets the runtime catch that and fall back to a scaled PNG, so the overdraw does not ship as a broken frame; a matching class would still be better.

storage.notes: / is a read-only squashfs with no /opt; /etc is an overlay on /data. /user-resource is the 6.3GB ext4 partition and carries the install, cache and logs. There is no printer_data directory on the device.
